name: Header
summary: The top bar of an app or a website — also called header, navbar or top bar. Brand, the site's links with the current page marked, actions, and on a phone a menu button that drops the links below the bar.

a11y.apg: No APG pattern: a banner is a landmark, not a widget. The role comes from the <header> element, so it is a banner only while it is not nested inside another sectioning element — which is how the AppShell places it. Keyboard behaviour belongs to what you put inside. The drawer toggle the shell injects is a button with popovertarget, and the browser is what supplies its aria-expanded. With `items`, the links sit in a <nav> named by `navLabel`, and the current one carries aria-current="page". Below 768px the menu button is a <button popovertarget> and the panel a <nav popover="auto"> — the same native mechanism as the AppShell drawer, with no script. The browser supplies the expanded state, and Escape and click-outside close the panel, in all three engines (measured 07/10/2026; see keyboardNote).
a11y.keyboardNote: Measured in a browser on 07/10/2026 (tests/visual/site-gar01-06.spec.ts, in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit), for the phone menu below 768px. Confirmed: Enter on the menu button opens and closes the panel; Escape closes it and returns focus to the button when it was opened from the keyboard; Tab moves into the panel right after the button in Chromium and Firefox. In WebKit, Tab does not reach links anywhere on a page by default (a Safari preference), so there the spec checks that the panel's first link is visible and takes focus; a button inside the same kind of popover is reached by Tab in WebKit 26.5 (measured the same day). Not confirmed: after a CLICK in WebKit, Escape closes the panel but focus goes to the page body, because WebKit does not focus a clicked button. Space is not declared: no spec measures it. Without `items` the Header owns no keys: the keyboard belongs to what you put inside.

props.name: variant
props.description: The skin. floating is a detached card; flush merges into the background so the bar frames the window; pill is a centred capsule for a site header — not for a shell, because search plus density plus theme plus command do not fit in a capsule.

props.name: brand
props.description: The lockup. It lives here and not in the sidebar: the top crosses the full width and the side panel starts below it. Inside a shell this is also where the drawer toggle sits, injected before what you pass.

props.name: children
props.description: Everything beside the brand: sections, search, actions, account. Presentational — the bar never decides what collapses. It wraps by content, so text at 200% breaks it to a second line instead of overflowing; hide what is secondary with hide-below-md/lg.

props.name: divider
props.description: Only on `flush` (B-07): a hairline under the bar. flush has the page's background and sticks to the top, so without a line the content scrolls under it with nothing saying where the bar ends.

props.name: items
props.description: The website's links (GAR-01, 07/10/2026) — the same list the Sidebar and the BottomNav take, so the app keeps one menu. Uses id, label, href and render (the router link); sub-items, icon and onClick are ignored: the bar is flat. Below 768px they leave the bar and drop into the menu panel.

props.name: current
props.description: The id of the current page's item: it gets aria-current="page", the highlight colour and the medium weight, in the bar and in the menu panel.

props.name: actions
props.description: What sits on the right: search, a call to action, the account. It stays in the bar on a phone too.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: How far the bar's content grows, on the Container's scale, so the bar lines up with the page below it. Without it, the bar keeps its own padding.

props.name: navLabel
props.description: The navigation's name for screen readers. Pass it in the page's language.

props.name: menuLabel
props.description: The phone menu button's name for screen readers. Pass it in the page's language. In an app with client-side routing the panel does not close by itself on a page change: give the Header a key that changes with the route.

props.name: menuId
props.description: The id of the phone menu panel, which the button points at with popovertarget. Change it only when a page has two website headers: each one needs its own.
